body.x: The year 2012 will be a noteworthy one for global spending on consumer electronics, with worldwide tech product demand projected to account for more than $1 trillion in sales for the first time ever. The figure signals a bounceback of sorts from the 2009 figure of $824 billion spent during the height of the recession.

That was the bottom-line assessment offered in a joint statistical presentation by Consumer Electronics Association(CEA) director of industry analysis Steve Koenig and GfK Boutique Research global business director Steve Bambridge in Las Vegas, on the Sunday preceding the opening of the 2012 International CES.

Koenig said while 2011 growth had been driven mainly by emerging markets, different regions exhibited growth spurts at different times. For example, Latin America, which accounted for 34 percent of demand in 2010, cooled in 2011 to just 11 percent, while Eastern European demand “popped” to 18 percent in 2011 versus 11 percent in 2010.

Despite the impressive overall figure projected for 2012, world CE sales growth dipped to eight percent in 2011 from 12 percent in 2010, and it is expected to slow to just five percent in 2012, with developed markets accounting for the main drag on sales.

“Smartphones and tablets are the growth stories of 2011,” said Bambridge, pointing out that most other product categories contracted last year. He said the worldwide industry could expect to see more of the same in terms of 2012 category growth, but that tablet PC and smartphone categories could be slightly down in developed markets, where their penetration was highest. However, he said 2012 sales projections worldwide for tablet PCs had recently been revised upward to 96 million units, and could easily exceed 100 million. “There’s still lots of growth in the category, and a long way to go in other markets” besides developed markets, he said.
